summary: Bear Hill tower in Middlesex Fells: the register lists a 70-foot steel lookout used 1919-1926; a 2011 blog and a travel guide describe other towers; closed to climbers since 2023 per guides.

facts.design: Sources disagree: the register describes a 70-foot steel tower; a 2011 blog found a reinforced concrete tower beside a working water holder
facts.status_note: Sources disagree on which structure is on the hill. A 2011 blog saw a standing concrete tower; the goxplr guide says the tower remains visible from several trails. No current site visit found
facts.agency: Massachusetts Department of Conservation and Recreation (DCR)

access.note: Closed to climbers. A trail guide says Friends of the Fells lists the tower as closed; the goxplr guide says officials closed access in 2023 for safety and a chain-link fence surrounds the base. The trail still goes to the base

events.note: goxplr: new steel observation tower completed late 1908 by the Metropolitan District Commission. The same guide dates the first, wooden tower to the late 1890s (year not given)
Blog, citing Friends of the Fells: wooden tower replaced by a reinforced concrete tower in the year an electric trolley station opened at Sheepfold
Blog visit: concrete tower beside a functioning water holder; visitor climbed the spiral stairs
goxplr: officials closed access to the tower citing safety concerns; fence around base; entrance sealed

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Forest Lookouts page and the Former Fire Lookout Sites register place the tower in Medford, Middlesex County. The blog and the goxplr guide call the town Stoneham. The story gives both names and uses Middlesex County, on which all sources agree
The register gives 70 feet (21.3 m); the goxplr guide gives about 60 feet. No height is recorded because the two are not reconciled

notes_for_editor: Probable duplicate of us-ma-medford-bear-hill (FFLOS US 38, Medford Bear Hill Tower Site: same 70-foot steel register entry, Bear Hill, Middlesex County). The coordinates differ: this record 42.50787, -71.09894 versus the FFLOS point 42.46567, -71.1065, about 4.7 km apart. Recommend merging; not done here. The blog attributes its 1910 account to Friends of the Fells, but the Friends of the Fells history page read does not contain it. The goxplr guide is a travel site; its 2023 closure claim rests on it and the trail guide, which cites Friends of the Fells, and no DCR statement was found. A Forest Fire Lookout Association post seen only as a search snippet gives 1916 as the first fire-tower use and says one of two Medford towers was used as a fire lookout for a short time; the post could not be read, so it is not used. The register's 70-foot figure and the goxplr 60-foot figure are not reconciled. No photos added.
